title: What If You Only Slept Six Hours a Night?

scenes.text: What if you only slept six hours every night? You wouldn't feel the worst part.
Scientists in Pennsylvania limited volunteers to six hours in bed for two weeks straight.
Every day, their attention lapses piled up. There was no point where they leveled off.
By the end, they performed like people who had stayed awake for one to two nights straight.
Yet they rated themselves only a little sleepy. They believed they had adapted.
So six hours doesn't feel like a problem. That's exactly why it is one.

description:
In a 2003 University of Pennsylvania study published in Sleep, 48 adults were restricted to 4, 6 or 8 hours in bed for 14 days, or kept awake for three nights.
The 6-hour group's attention lapses rose steadily with no plateau, reaching levels equivalent to up to two nights of total sleep deprivation, while their own sleepiness ratings rose only slightly.
